title: HB430 (2023 Regular): RELATING TO FIREARMS.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Hawaii) (gun-policy Stage 5, Hawaii); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Hawaii text (Introduced, official copy, https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/sessions/session2023/bills/HB430_.HTM; sha256 755ce1311ce5dfa2fbfb94a68eb10e38dbddbf278c46c4dc4df260e85712aa63)
provenance.note: Introduced text (as filed); no passage vote on record. Effective date written as July 1, 2050 (placeholder). The bill strikes the 'exceptional case ... reason to fear injury' showing in 134-9(a) and changes 'may' to 'shall' for chiefs of police issuing permits and licenses (struck words, described not quoted); it also strikes the 'enclosed container' definition in favor of 'locked container'. Same bill carried over into the second year; text identical.

SECTION 1 (new §134-A): (a) Except as provided in subsections (b) through (e), a person granted a license to carry a concealed firearm under section 134-9 shall not knowingly carry a firearm on or into any of the following sensitive locations: (1) A school, college, university, or other educational institution, or any school bus; (4) A bar or restaurant where alcohol is served, and any other site or facility where alcohol is sold for consumption on the premises; (6) A courthouse, courtroom, or any other premises used to conduct judicial or court administrative proceedings or functions; (12) A public or private hospital or hospital affiliate, mental health facility, nursing home, medical office, urgent care facility, or other place at which medical services are customarily provided; or (13) Private property, including but not limited to residential, commercial, industrial, agricultural, institutional, or undeveloped property, unless the owner has provided express consent or clearly and conspicuously posts a sign at the entrance of the building or on the premises indicating that licensees are permitted to carry firearms on the property. (f) Any person violating subsection (a) shall be: (1) Guilty of a misdemeanor;

SECTION 2 (HRS 134-1): "Locked container" means a secure container that is fully enclosed and locked by a padlock, keylock, combination lock, or similar locking device.
SECTION 3 (HRS 134-2): The issuing authority shall not issue a permit to acquire the ownership of a firearm to any person where the issuance would not be in the interest of the public health, safety, or welfare because the person is found to be lacking the essential character or temperament necessary to be entrusted with a firearm.
SECTION 5 (HRS 134-9): (4) Not be under indictment for, or have waived indictment for, or have been bound over to the circuit court for, or have been convicted in this State or elsewhere of having committed in the previous ten years: (A) A firearm offense punishable as a misdemeanor under this chapter; (B) Operating a vehicle under the influence of an intoxicant under section 291E-61; (f) A fee of $10 shall be charged for each license granted under this section.
